term: exact-length directed path and iterated modalities
definition: ExactPath F n a b has a Mathlib Quiver.Path from a to b in the explicit F.toQuiver with length exactly n. Zero length means a=b, not a self-edge; successor length decomposes into an original access edge followed by an exact n-path. Formula.iterBox and iterDiamond repeat their modal constructor n times, with zero repetitions the unchanged formula. Their Holds semantics universally and existentially quantify, respectively, over endpoints of paths of exactly that length.
note: Uses the existing Mathlib path length rather than hand-rolled reachability. Exact length is not arbitrary finite reachability, shortest distance, an infinite path, analytic convergence or temporal duration.
